name: metal0
_comment_payout_onchain: payoutAddress is where THIS BOX sweeps earnings; the chain does not know it. To also run YOUR OWN apps here for free (ledger rev 12), publish it: `enclave host declare-payout` sends EnclaveRegistry.setPayoutWallet from that wallet, and deployments it owns are then charged nothing on this enclave (a paid app's publisher fee still applies). It must come from the wallet itself - the operator key cannot declare it, which is what stops a box naming a stranger.

_autoUpdate_optional._note: Pull-based release tracking — the self-hosted answer to 'merge to main and the Tinfoil fleet updates'. Enable the timer: cp metal/systemd/enclave-metal-update.* ~/.config/systemd/user/ && systemctl --user enable --now enclave-metal-update.timer
_autoUpdate_optional._onlyWhenIdle: true (default) waits for the box to have no tenants before restarting: a restart relaunches every tenant AND costs one ACME issuance per app-zone hostname (initramfs guest, nothing persists; Let's Encrypt allows 5 per 168h per name)
_autoUpdate_optional._maxDeferSec: ceiling on that wait — a box that always has a tenant must not fall permanently behind. Default 21600 (6h)
_autoUpdate_optional._healthGraceSec: how long the new image gets to come back healthy before it is rolled back and updates halt. Default 300

_comment_ggml: ggml engine tuning for the tenants this box serves (rename to "ggml"). Keys are camelCase knobs or full ENCLAVE_GGML_* names; only the tuning ones pass (nCtx, maxSessions, nBatch, nUbatch, kvCacheType, kvCacheTypeV, flashAttn, nThreads) and anything else is dropped with a line in the guest log - placement knobs are deliberately not settable, since the manager sets N_GPU_LAYERS itself and a wrong value fails the tenant at launch. maxSessions defaults to 8 here (the hosted fleet's number) and you rarely want less: a session is a sequence handle into ONE shared KV pool, so slots cost no memory of their own, and at the engine's own default of 1 a single chat's internal passes queue behind its main answer until the app gives up ('waiting for a free slot'). nCtx is the opposite - it SIZES that pool, so it is the knob that costs RAM: the whole window is allocated up front and shared by all sessions of a graph. Unset = the engine's 8192, which is small for a chat app; the hosted fleet runs 180224 at q8_0. Price it before raising it (KV bytes/token = 2 x kv_layers x n_kv_heads x head_dim x element size) and remember a CPU-served model pays it out of node RAM. A single deployment can override its own window with the `nnCtx` app-config key instead. nThreads is CPU compute threads for text models: unset = every vCPU the guest has (the right answer in a CVM), and it exists only to pin BELOW that - before it existed the engine silently ran llama's 4-thread default, which is a 4x cliff on a 16-vCPU box serving on cores.
_comment_shielded_tuning: tenantEnv: SHIELDED_* environment for the GUEST tenant's engine (only SHIELDED_* names survive; anything else is dropped by the guest and again by the wasm-manager). SHIELDED_SPIN_US = microseconds the tenant polls the socket for the worker's reply before it blocks and its vCPU halts; 0 (default) = block at once. workerEnv: environment for the HOST-side worker process; SHIELDED_WORKER_SPIN_US = the same poll on the worker's side for the next request. Both cost a spinning core while they poll. Either can be changed with a launcher restart and no release; the guest one needs a release that carries this launcher's fw_cfg plumbing.
_comment_guest_haltpoll: cpuidle-haltpoll in the guest kernel. ON by default: an idle vCPU polls for a bounded, self-tuning window (guest_halt_poll_ns, 200 us) before it halts, so the shielded worker's reply lands on a running vCPU instead of paying a VM exit + injected interrupt per exchange (~49 per decoded token; 152 us each in the CVM vs 46 on the host loopback). COST: every idle vCPU may burn its host core for up to that window after each piece of work before halting; the window shrinks to zero when wakeups stop landing in it. false = plain HLT. An object tunes the governor without a release: { "ns": 200000, "growStart": 50000, "grow": 2, "shrink": 2, "allowShrink": true } (nanoseconds; kernel defaults shown). Rides fw_cfg, never the measured cmdline; the image only has to carry the driver (metal >= the release with metal/guest/init's haltpoll block).
_comment_shielded: Sell GPU work WITHOUT putting the GPU in the enclave. priceUsdHr is this box's ask for a WHOLE shielded card per hour, and it is only advertised once the boot probe passes: no pass, no capacity, no price. The card stays on the host, outside the measurement; the guest reaches the worker at 10.0.2.2:<port> and sends it public weights and one-time-padded activations only. See docs/shielded-inference.md and shielded/README.md. Requires python3 + torch + triton on the HOST, not in the guest. Omit unless the box has a CUDA card.
_comment: mode: snp | tdx | dev. dev = plain KVM (no attestation) for bring-up. hostfwd exposes guest ports on host loopback for local testing; production reachability is the fleet tunnel (relayUrl), so hostfwd can be empty. AUTH: set tunnelToken to attach via the relay's committed token allowlist (first-party boxes); OR leave tunnelToken empty to attach PERMISSIONLESSLY by proving your SEV-SNP measurement is on the relay's METAL_ALLOWED_MEASUREMENTS allowlist (metal/PROTOCOL.md). egressHelper (rename to "egressHelper") is only needed on sandboxed hosts whose user-net can't NAT externally; a normal seller box dials the relay directly.
_comment_pricing: WHAT YOU CHARGE (rename to priceCpuUsdHr / priceGpuUsdHr): USD per hour for a FULL node and a FULL card. This is THE price on a rev-8 ledger, not a floor: it is published in your EnclaveRegistry entry, and when you claim a deployment the chain charges its owner exactly your price times the shares they bought - a 17% CPU share of a $3.00/hr node pays $0.51/hr, of which you keep runnerBps (80% today). Every deployment carries its own hourly ceiling (maxRate6), so work whose owner capped below your price is not offered to you (claim reverts 'over rate cap') - it waits for someone cheaper. Change the price any time: the guest republishes it on its next heartbeat, and live leases keep the price they were claimed at. Unset = the fleet defaults ($3.00/node-hr, $6.00/card-hr). priceGpuUsdHr only applies when this really is a GPU enclave (gpuCount > 0 with a card passed through); on a CPU-only box it is ignored, because advertising a price for hardware you cannot serve sells work you can never run.
_comment_volumes: ATTESTED MODEL VOLUMES (rename to volumes / volumeStore): big read-only weights served the way Tinfoil's Modelwrap serves them, but built by you. Each volume is one file (ext4 + an appended dm-verity hash tree) made with `node metal/volumes.mjs build <name> --src <model tree>`; the launcher attaches it read-only and the GUEST sets dm-verity up itself, so every block a tenant reads is hash-checked in the CVM. Use "*" to attach every volume in the store. The set's digest is launched into the CPU's HOST_DATA field, so every attestation report this enclave produces names exactly which models it carries (metal/verify.mjs checks it) - while the launch measurement, which allowlists pin, stays the release's. Deployments then attach them by name via the console volume picker or their config CID.
_comment_acme: In-enclave app TLS: the guest keeps every private key inside the CVM and builds the CSR there. DEFAULT: the CSR goes to the platform certificate service (certsApi, default = the API relay origin derived from relayUrl, e.g. https://api.enclave.host), which holds the CA account (ZeroSSL, Let's Encrypt fallback), answers DNS-01, paces the fleet against the CA rate limits, and returns a certificate only for <label>.app.enclave.host names whose lease this box holds on-chain (your operator key signs the request). NO per-box CA credential is needed: a FIRST-PARTY box config.json should NOT carry acmeEabKid/acmeEabHmac any more - remove them (the launcher refuses to forward them without the flag below, and the fw_cfg file they used to ride in is 0600 since eed7f2fd precisely because it carried them). EXCEPTION: a seller who wants to mint directly from their OWN free ZeroSSL account (Developer page -> EAB credentials) renames the acmeEab* pair AND sets acmeBringYourOwn: true; then the in-guest ACME client mints via ZeroSSL first, Let's Encrypt second, and the platform service is the fallback. Without the flag the pair is ignored with a warning.
_comment_earning: EARNING (Phase C, metal/PROTOCOL.md): rename registryKey/payoutAddress (drop the _..._optional wrapper) to sell hosting. registryKey = a fresh EOA private key funded with a few dollars of Base ETH for gas; the guest supervisor uses it to register this enclave, claim funded deployments, and collect the runner share the EnclaveDeployments ledger (schema rev 7+) escrows for whoever holds each lease. payoutAddress = YOUR wallet; accrued USDC earnings are auto-withdrawn to it once they clear EARNINGS_MIN_USDC (default $5). Set publicUrl to the relay-routed URL (https://api.enclave.host/t/<name>) so the registry entry is dialable through the tunnel. Both keys ride fw_cfg like tunnelToken: out-of-band, never part of the measurement.
